text:
sara_g: Heads-up — there's an OSS advisory landing for grpc and golang-jwt plus a net/http path normalization note. Need quick triage: hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private images. Any immediate exploitability concerns?

alex_h: Thanks. Can you paste links to the advisories?

sara_g: Link to grpc CVE: https://example.com/advisories/CVE-2026-GRPC (priv-esc via metadata parsing).
Also golang-jwt: https://example.com/advisories/CVE-2026-JWT (signature validation edge case).
And stdlib note: https://example.com/advisories/NETHTTP-2026 (path normalization leading to 404->200 mismatch).

morgan_r: Skimming — grpc fix is a pure Go patch (minor). jwt is a parser fix, likely exploit requires crafted tokens and the app to accept unverified tokens. net/http one affects servers that use CleanPath + custom routing; our router uses gorilla/mux but we do some internal path munging in edge-proxy.

alex_h: Repro attempt: ran unit tests + a small fuzzer against the auth path. No immediate token acceptance bug locally, but I saw an edge case where an empty kid header caused a panic in jwt lib.

paul_devops: CI ran golangci-lint + tests across images and one Dedicated canary failed on auth unit tests after bumping grpc locally. Posting CI output below:

ci-bot: CI: failed tests in repo/redwood/auth (go1.20 linux/amd64)
```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
goroutine 12 [running]:
github.com/golang-jwt/jwt.(*Parser).parseHeader(...)
	/repo/pkg/mod/github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v3.2.0/parser.go:72
redwood/auth/token_test.go:45 +0x145
```

morgan_r: That lines up with the CVE description — older jwt versions can panic on missing header values. Patch exists in v3.2.2 per the advisory.

alex_h: Proposed minimal action: pin+update go.mod to patched versions, run full integration tests in staging, then canary rollout to hosted. For Dedicated/Private we need a backport/hotpatch plan because customers may vendor or pin older versions.

morgan_r: Agreed. Suggested go.mod diff:
```
- github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v3.2.0
+ github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v3.2.2
- google.golang.org/grpc v1.56.0
+ google.golang.org/grpc v1.56.4
```
Commands to run locally:
```
go get github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v3.2.2 google.golang.org/grpc@v1.56.4
go mod tidy
go test ./...  # run unit + integration
```

paul_devops: For Dedicated we should prepare a hotpatch image (branch + pinned module) and schedule a 30-min maintenance window. For Private, produce a patch bundle and guidance: replace directives or updated vendor tarball. Also update our SBOM and compliance docs.

alex_h: I can open the PR with the module bumps and a short test matrix. Will include a gosum verification and CHANGELOG note referencing the CVEs.

sara_g: Please also add an eval / smoke prompt for jwt acceptance to Redwood Optimize: that will alert on regressions where token parsing differs post-patch.

morgan_r: One more note: net/http issue — our edge-proxy uses path cleaning in a small helper. I'll audit edge-proxy and put a small patch to canonicalize before routing, plus add a regression test.

ci-bot: CI: new PR template check passed, dependency scanner flagged the CVEs and auto-attached links.

alex_h: Assigned: @alex_h => PR + staging canary, @morgan_r => edge-proxy audit + tests, @paul_devops => Dedicated hotpatch image & Private guidance. Target: PR by EOD, staging canary tomorrow morning.

sara_g: Thanks — prioritize hosted API first (fastest mitigation), Dedicated next, Private guidance same-day. Marking as P0 and notifying security oncall. :lock: :warning:
